tldr: Unknown rough selection has an exact design-robust phase diagram at a CATE boundary. With an unknown covariate density bounded above and below near zero, a total same-cell pair ratio and a public bias-plus-Chebyshev radius attain both minimax absolute risk and \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval expected length at exponent \(r_\alpha=\min\{1/4,(\alpha+1/8)/(2\alpha+5/4)\}\). The unique elbow is \(\alpha=3/8\), with no logarithmic loss; the rough endpoint \(\alpha=1/4\) is \(n^{-3/14}\), while the supplied-propensity benchmark is \(n^{-1/4}\). Matching lower bounds are witnessed by legal full-support uniform-design Bernoulli sign laws, an explicit subclass of the bounded-density model.
gap: Published pointwise CATE minimax theory uses overlap conditions that exclude a linearly vanishing propensity, while published weak-overlap theory studies average targets or single response regressions. No located result determines all-procedure pointwise risk and honest interval length when selection vanishes linearly and its absolute modulus is rougher than the treatment contrast.
